question.problem:
Consider the surface integral of the function $f(x,y,z)={z}^{2},$ where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=x+\sqrt{2}y$ for $-1\le x\le 2$ and $-1\le y\le 2.$
This surface integral can be written as a repeated integral, as shown below. 

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}\boxed{}\,\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=g(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f(x,y,z)$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

For the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂x}=\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+\sqrt{2}y)=1,
$$

and

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂y}=\frac{∂}{∂y}(x+\sqrt{2}y)=\sqrt{2}.
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(1)}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2(x+\sqrt{2}y)^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}\,2({x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}+2\sqrt{2}xy)\,\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
